definition.value: Regular dummy equal to 1 when the EQ-5D-5L health state presented to the respondent has the anxiety/depression dimension at severity level 4; the omitted category is level 1 (no problems) on that dimension. The EQ-5D-5L has five dimensions (mobility, self-care, usual activities, pain/discomfort, anxiety/depression) each with five severity levels.

timing.value: Presented to the respondent during the computer-assisted personal interview (October 2018 - November 2019); each respondent valued ten cTTO health states and seven DCE pairs in one interview.

outcome.label: Utility decrement (β) of an EQ-5D-5L dimension level, estimated from the observed composite time trade-off (cTTO) value of the health state

definition.value: Table 2 reports β coefficients that "should be read as utility decrements in the calculation of health-related quality of life"; a health state's value is 1 minus the sum of the decrements of its dimension levels (worked example, p. 586: state 13224 has U = 1-0-0.050-0.033-0.048-0.430 = 0.439). The underlying elicited quantity is the observed composite time trade-off value of the health state, on a scale from − 1 to 1 in 0.05 increments (1 = full health, 0 = dead), censored at − 1; the model is estimated on random-effects Tobit model estimated on the cTTO data alone, which takes explicit account of the censoring of observed cTTO values at − 1.

timing.value: Elicited in the valuation interview itself; the cTTO task values living ten years in the health state, with lead-time TTO adding a further ten years for states considered worse than dead.

units.value: EQ-5D-5L utility decrement, in units of the value scale on which 1 = full health and 0 = dead

estimand.target_population: The adult (18+) Danish general population, whose preferences the value set is intended to represent.

population.description: 1014 adults (18+) from the Danish general population interviewed in the Danish EQ-5D-5L valuation study, each valuing ten EQ-5D-5L health states by cTTO and seven pairs by DCE.
population.selection: Statistics Denmark drew a randomly chosen sample representative on age (> 18 years), gender, education and geographical region and supplied contact information on 4585 individuals, invited in blocks of about 500; a Danish market research company panel was added half-way through, selecting respondents by the same principles and excluding anyone who had taken a health survey in the previous 6 months. Of 1052 interviews carried out, 5 were dropped with two interviewers, 12 for software issues/withdrawn consent/cognitive or emotional issues and 21 for not contributing both cTTO and DCE data, leaving 1014.

identification.source_of_variation: Experimental variation in the EQ-5D-5L health states respondents were asked to value: a standardized blocked EQ-VT design in which 86 health states were valued in blocks of ten by cTTO (and 196 pairs in 28 blocks of seven by DCE), with respondents randomly assigned to a block and randomised order of states.

key_assumptions.assumption: Additive main-effects specification: the value of a health state is the sum of the decrements of its dimension levels, with no interactions between dimensions.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper states the EQ-VT was designed for maximum power to identify main effects and that no interaction effects were included or investigated; the worked example on p. 586 adds decrements across dimensions. Not tested.

key_assumptions.assumption: The censoring of observed cTTO values at − 1, imposed by the construction of the EQ-VT, is correctly handled by the censored (Tobit) specification, and the distributional assumptions of that model hold.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated in Sect. 2.5.1; the paper argues the Tobit model is conceptually preferred to the GLS model for this reason. The distributional form is not tested.

key_assumptions.assumption: Respondents' stated cTTO valuations measure the preferences of the adult Danish general population, and the achieved sample is representative of that population.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Table 1 compares the study sample with Statistics Denmark figures for the adult Danish general population on gender, age, marital status, education, work status, income and region; the paper concedes slight under-representation of 18-24-year-olds and of the lowest educational level.

key_assumptions.assumption: The estimation sample is conditioned on respondent behaviour: cTTO observations for health states a respondent flagged in the feedback module as inappropriately ranked were dropped (712 observations), and respondents who did not contribute both cTTO and DCE data (n = 21) were dropped.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated in Sect. 2.5 and Sect. 3.2. A sensitivity analysis reintroducing the 712 flagged observations left the estimates qualitatively unchanged (data not shown).

claims.statement: The heteroscedastic censored hybrid model gives EQ-5D-5L health state 55555 (the most severe state) a value of − 0.757, the lowest score in the Danish value set and below 0 (dead).

treatment.label: EQ-5D-5L health state 55555 (level 5, the most severe level, on all five dimensions)

definition.value: The worst possible EQ-5D-5L health state: level 5 on mobility, self-care, usual activities, pain/discomfort and anxiety/depression. It was the one severe state included in every cTTO block, so all 1014 respondents valued it.

timing.value: Valued in the EQ-VT interview (October 2018 - November 2019).

outcome.label: Predicted value (utility) of the health state in the Danish EQ-5D-5L value set

definition.value: The value assigned to a health state by the final Danish value set, computed as 1 minus the sum of the utility decrements of its dimension levels from the heteroscedastic censored hybrid model; 1 = full health, 0 = dead, negative = worse than dead. Modelling was used because only 86 of the 3125 states were valued directly.

timing.value: A model prediction, not measured at any date.

units.value: EQ-5D-5L value (utility), where 1 = full health and 0 = dead

magnitude.interpretation: the lowest score in the Danish value set; the 5L value set has a lower value for the worst possible health state than the Danish EQ-5D-3L and crosswalk value sets (− 0.624)

estimand.target_population: The adult (18+) Danish general population whose preferences the value set represents.

population.description: The 3125 EQ-5D-5L health states valued by the Danish value set, estimated from 1014 adult Danish general-population respondents.
population.selection: Predictions for all 3125 states from a model fitted to the 86 directly valued states; state 55555 was valued by all 1014 respondents.

identification.source_of_variation: The hybrid model's estimated utility decrements, applied additively to the dimension levels of state 55555.

key_assumptions.assumption: Additive main effects: the value of state 55555 is 1 minus the sum of the five level-5 decrements, with no interaction between dimensions.
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper's own worked example of the prediction rule (p. 586) and the statement that no interaction effects were included or investigated. Not tested.

key_assumptions.assumption: The hybrid model's parameters, estimated on 86 directly valued states, extrapolate to all 3125 EQ-5D-5L states.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated as the reason for modelling (Sect. 2.5.1). No out-of-sample validation is reported.

evidence.annotation: Distribution of mean observed cTTO value (n = 10,140) by severity level of the health state. Severity level is calculated as the sum score of the dimension levels

outcomes_examined_not_reported: Heteroscedastic conditional logit model for the DCE data (data not shown)
Sensitivity analysis reintroducing the 712 incorrectly ranked cTTO states (data not shown)
Experimental DCE valuation task (reported separately)
Questions on attitudes towards prioritisation in the Danish healthcare system (reported separately)
GLS random intercept model, conditional logit model and hybrid model without censoring (reported only in Online Supplementary Material 3)

anchor_quote.text: Figure 1 shows that mean cTTO values decreased with increasing health state severity as expected

claims.statement: Across the 86 directly valued EQ-5D-5L health states, predicted value of the health state from the heteroscedastic censored hybrid model (ctto + dce data) is strongly positively associated with predicted value of the health state from the random-effects tobit model (ctto data) (Fig. 3, panel "Y:Tobit_GLS X:Hybrid II(-1) het").

treatment.label: Predicted value of the health state from the heteroscedastic censored hybrid model (cTTO + DCE data)

definition.value: Model-predicted EQ-5D-5L value for each of the 86 health states directly valued in the cTTO task; plotted on the x-axis of this panel of Fig. 3.

timing.value: A model prediction, not measured at any date.

outcome.label: Predicted value of the health state from the random-effects Tobit model (cTTO data)

definition.value: Model-predicted EQ-5D-5L value for the same 86 health states; plotted on the y-axis of this panel of Fig. 3. Conditional logit (DCE) predictions are on an arbitrary, unanchored scale.

timing.value: A model prediction, not measured at any date.

magnitude.interpretation: the paper reads the scatter plots as showing strong correlation and similar rank orderings of health states, which it takes as support for the hybrid model's key assumption that the two parameter vectors differ only by a multiplicative constant

estimand.target_population: The 86 EQ-5D-5L health states valued directly in the cTTO task.

population.description: The 86 EQ-5D-5L health states directly valued in the cTTO task of the Danish valuation study; predictions from models fitted to the 1014 respondents' cTTO and DCE data.
population.selection: Restricted to the 86 states valued directly; the remaining 3039 states are predicted but not plotted.

identification.source_of_variation: Differences between the 86 health states in the severity profile valued.

key_assumptions.assumption: The plot is read as support for the hybrid model's key assumption that the cTTO and DCE parameter vectors are equal up to a multiplicative constant: "If the plots show a straight line, this supports the key assumption."
key_assumptions.supported_by: The scatter plots of Fig. 3 themselves; no formal test is reported.

threats_discussed: DCE values lie on an arbitrary scale rather than one anchored at 0 (death) and 1 (full health), so the logit predictions are not directly comparable in level

estimator.value: Scatter plot of predicted values, with no fitted statistic reported

estimation.specification: Predictions for the 86 directly valued health states from (i) a random-effects Tobit model on cTTO data, (ii) a conditional logit model on DCE data and (iii) the heteroscedastic censored hybrid model, plotted against each other.

source_table.value: Figure 3, panel "Y:Tobit_GLS X:Hybrid II(-1) het" (p. 586)

ambiguities: No numerical measure of association is printed; the sign is the paper's verbal reading ("strong correlation") of the scatter plot.
This is an agreement-between-models claim, not a claim about any person-level outcome; the edge is recorded only because the paper uses it as evidence for the hybrid model's key assumption.

evidence.annotation: Scatter plot of the predicted values for the 86 health states valued in cTTO using a random-effects Tobit model (cTTO data), the logit model (DCE data), and heteroscedastic censored hybrid model (cTTO and DCE data).
